subject: Cognitive Science
title: Bottom-Up vs Top-Down
description: Learn Bottom-Up vs Top-Down in one minute.

hook.text: A fire alarm grabs your attention. Searching for keys in a messy drawer takes effort. Different systems.

buildup.text: Bottom-up attention is involuntary—bright colors, loud bangs, and sudden motion capture you.

discovery.text: Top-down attention is voluntary—you direct the spotlight based on goals and expectations.

twist.text: The two systems compete. A text notification can hijack top-down focus in milliseconds.

climax.text: Experts learn to resist bottom-up capture. Surgeons ignore beeping monitors they've deemed safe.

punchline.text: Some attention is grabbed; some is given.

quiz.question: Which type of attention is involuntary?

details.summary: Attention can be captured involuntarily by salient stimuli like a loud noise (bottom-up) or directed voluntarily toward a goal like searching for a friend in a crowd (top-down). These two systems interact constantly, and their balance determines what enters awareness.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding bottom-up versus top-down attention explains why distractions are so powerful and how goals can override sensory salience with effort and practice.
takeaways: Bottom-up attention is stimulus-driven and involuntary
Top-down attention is goal-driven and voluntary
Real-world attention involves constant interplay of both systems

faq.question: Which type of attention is stronger?
faq.answer: Bottom-up capture is faster and initially stronger because it evolved to detect threats. However, top-down control can override it with sustained effort. In daily life, top-down goals guide most behavior, but sudden salient events can hijack attention instantly.

faq.question: How do advertisers exploit bottom-up attention?
faq.answer: Advertisers use bright colors, motion, sudden sounds, and faces to trigger involuntary bottom-up capture. Pop-up ads, autoplay videos, and notification badges all exploit the same stimulus-driven alerting system that originally evolved for predator detection.
